from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        # Create elements
        node_a = Dot(color=WHITE)

        self.place_at_grid(node_b, 'D2')
        self.place_at_grid(node_c, 'D4')
        
        label_a = Text("A", font_size=24).next_to(node_a, UP)
        label_b = Text("B", font_size=24).next_to(node_b, LEFT)
        label_c = Text("C", font_size=24).next_to(node_c, RIGHT)

        path_ab = Line(node_a.get_center(), node_b.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        path_bc = Line(node_b.get_center(), node_c.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        path_ac = Line(node_a.get_center(), node_c.get_center(), color=WHITE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FF00"), Create(node_a), Create(node_b), Create(node_c), Write(label_a), Write(label_b), Write(label_c))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"), Create(path_ab.copy().set_color("#FFFF00")), Create(path_bc.copy().set_color("#FFFFFF")), Create(path_ac.copy().set_color("#FF0000")))
        label_0 = Text("0", font_size=24, color="#FFFF00").next_to(path_ab, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        label_1 = Text("1", font_size=24, color="#FFFFFF").next_to(path_bc, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        label_2 = Text("2", font_size=24, color="#FF0000").next_to(path_ac, UP, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Write(label_0), Write(label_1), Write(label_2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Constrained Hanoi limits moves to adjacent pegs.",
            "Moves A to B are zero.",
            "Moves B to C are one.",
            "Illegal moves are represented by two.",
            "Legal paths exclude the digit two."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Constrained Towers of Hanoi", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define Pegs
        peg_a = Circle(radius=0.3, color=WHITE).set_fill(WHITE, opacity=0.3)
        peg_b = Circle(radius=0.3, color=WHITE).set_fill(WHITE, opacity=0.3)
        peg_c = Circle(radius=0.3, color=WHITE).set_fill(WHITE, opacity=0.3)
        
        label_a = Text("A", font_size=20).next_to(peg_a, DOWN)
        label_b = Text("B", font_size=20).next_to(peg_b, DOWN)
        label_c = Text("C", font_size=20).next_to(peg_c, DOWN)
        
        pegs = VGroup(peg_a, peg_b, peg_c, label_a, label_b, label_c)
        self.place_at_grid(peg_a, "B1")
        self.place_at_grid(peg_b, "B3")
        self.place_at_grid(peg_c, "B5")
        label_a.move_to(self.grid["C1"])
        label_b.move_to(self.grid["C3"])
        label_c.move_to(self.grid["C5"])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(pegs))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)
        line_ab = Line(peg_a.get_center(), peg_b.get_center(), color=GREEN)
        arrow_ab = Arrow(start=peg_a.get_center(), end=peg_b.get_center(), color=GREEN)
        label_0 = Text("0 (A->B)", font_size=20, color=GREEN).next_to(line_ab, UP)
        self.play(Create(arrow_ab), Write(label_0))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        line_bc = Line(peg_b.get_center(), peg_c.get_center(), color=GREEN)
        arrow_bc = Arrow(start=peg_b.get_center(), end=peg_c.get_center(), color=GREEN)
        label_1 = Text("1 (B->C)", font_size=20, color=GREEN).next_to(line_bc, UP)
        self.play(Create(arrow_bc), Write(label_1))
        self.wait(1)

        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(RED)
        line_ac = Line(peg_a.get_center(), peg_c.get_center(), color=RED)
        arrow_ac = ArcBetweenPoints(peg_a.get_center(), peg_c.get_center(), angle=-TAU/6, color=RED)

        self.play(Create(arrow_ac), Write(label_2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        cross = Cross(arrow_ac, stroke_color=RED)
        self.play(Create(cross))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the Sierpinski Triangle", [
            "State space forms the Sierpinski Triangle.",
            "Recursive moves build fractal geometry.",
            "Each turn adds a ternary digit.",
            "Path-finding ant traverses triangle edges.",
            "Fractal structure emerges from recursion."
        ])

        # Colors for highlights
        colors = ["#FF5733", "#33FF57", "#3357FF", "#F3FF33", "#FF33F3"]

        # Sierpinski Triangle construction
        def sierpinski_triangle(order, side_length):
            if order == 0:
                return Triangle(color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.2).scale(side_length)
            else:
                sub = sierpinski_triangle(order - 1, side_length / 2)
                t = VGroup(
                    sub.copy().shift(UP * side_length * 0.433),
                    sub.copy().shift(LEFT * side_length * 0.5 + DOWN * side_length * 0.433),
                    sub.copy().shift(RIGHT * side_length * 0.5 + DOWN * side_length * 0.433)
                )
                return t

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        triangle = sierpinski_triangle(2, 2.0)
        self.place_in_area(triangle, "B2", "E5")
        self.play(Create(triangle), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(colors[0]))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(colors[1]))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        digits = VGroup(
            Text("0", font_size=20, color=YELLOW).move_to(self.grid["B3"]),
            Text("1", font_size=20, color=YELLOW).move_to(self.grid["D2"]),
            Text("2", font_size=20, color=YELLOW).move_to(self.grid["D4"])
        )
        self.play(FadeIn(digits), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(colors[2]))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        ant = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ant.svg")
        self.place_at_grid(ant, "C3", scale_factor=0.2)
        self.play(FadeIn(ant), self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(colors[3]))
        
        # Simple path for ant
        path = VMobject()
        path.set_points_as_corners([self.grid["B3"], self.grid["D2"], self.grid["D4"], self.grid["B3"]])
        self.play(MoveAlongPath(ant, path), run_time=3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(colors[4]))
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis: The Fractal Geometry of Computation", 
                          ["Hanoi moves map to Sierpinski points.", 
                           "Ternary addresses define fractal coordinates.", 
                           "Infinite recursion creates the geometric limit."])
        
        # Create visual elements
        # 3-disk Hanoi state diagram (simplified representation as a graph)
        nodes = [Dot(color=YELLOW) for _ in range(7)]
        for i, node in enumerate(nodes):
            self.place_at_grid(node, f"{['B2', 'B4', 'C1', 'C3', 'C5', 'D2', 'D4'][i]}")
            
        edges = VGroup(*[Line(nodes[i].get_center(), nodes[j].get_center(), color=YELLOW) 
                        for i, j in [(0, 2), (0, 3), (2, 5), (3, 5), (1, 3), (1, 4), (3, 6), (4, 6)]])
        
        hanoi_graph = VGroup(*nodes, edges)
        
        # 3rd iteration Sierpinski triangle
        def get_sierpinski_triangle(order=2):
            if order == 0:
                return Triangle(color=BLUE_C).scale(0.5)
            else:
                prev = get_sierpinski_triangle(order-1)
                t1 = prev.copy()
                t2 = prev.copy()
                t3 = prev.copy()
                VGroup(t1, t2, t3).arrange(UP, buff=0)
                return VGroup(t1, t2, t3)
        
        sierpinski = get_sierpinski_triangle(2).set_color(BLUE_C)
        self.place_in_area(sierpinski, 'A2', 'F5', scale_factor=0.6)
        sierpinski.set_opacity(0)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(hanoi_graph))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(sierpinski))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE_C)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(Transform(hanoi_graph, sierpinski))
        self.play(FadeOut(hanoi_graph))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Ternary Code of Sierpinski: From Towers of Hanoi to Fractals
outline.target_audience: University students (Computer Science or Discrete Mathematics)

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Logic of Base-3
sections.content: Introduce the ternary system (0, 1, 2) as the natural language of branching structures. Contrast with binary to show why ternary fits structures with three-way choices.
sections.example: A smart robot moving between three charging stations (A, B, C) where each step is represented by a digit (0, 1, or 2).

sections.title: The Constrained Towers of Hanoi
sections.content: Explain the variation where disks can only move between adjacent pegs (A↔B, B↔C). Reveal that the sequence of moves to solve this follows the ternary counting pattern.
sections.example: Representing disk movements as a sequence: 0 for A→B, 1 for B→C, 2 for A→C (an illegal jump). We show that the 'legal' path avoids digit 2, forming a self-similar path.

sections.title: Visualizing the Sierpinski Triangle
sections.content: Connect the Hanoi state space to the Sierpinski Triangle. As the number of disks increases, the state diagram converges to the Sierpinski gasket, illustrating how recursive movement forms fractal geometry.
sections.example: An animation showing a 'path-finding ant' traversing the edges of a Sierpinski triangle; each turn at a vertex corresponds to adding a digit in a ternary expansion.

sections.title: Synthesis: The Fractal Geometry of Computation
sections.content: Summarize the isomorphism: The set of legal moves in the constrained Hanoi problem is the graph of the Sierpinski triangle. Ternary counting serves as the coordinate system for this infinite fractal space.
sections.example: A visual overlay showing a 3-disk Hanoi state diagram perfectly mapping onto the 3rd iteration of a Sierpinski triangle, using colors to track the 'ternary address' of each position.
